    Instructor Notes

    Overall approach

    • Each episode page gives the concept and a short code walkthrough. The hands-on work happens in the three linked Colab notebooks (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced), each about 20 to 30 minutes.
    • In a 90 minute session, teach the episode page and the Beginner notebook together, then let learners continue with the Intermediate notebook. Treat Advanced notebooks as take home material.
    • Each episode has a theory part (concepts, assumptions, interpretation and pitfalls) and a code part. The third challenge in each episode is conceptual and works well as a pair discussion while a slow cell runs.
    • Ask everyone to Save a copy in Drive before running anything. Most “lost work” questions come from editing the read only original.
    • Notebooks were last tested (October 2026) with OSMnx 2.1, scikit-learn 1.9, rasterio 1.5, libpysal 4.15 and esda 2.10. OSMnx 2.0 removed geometries_from_place and utils_graph; older tutorials online still use them.

    Episode by episode

    Geoprocessing in Python and in QGIS

    • The two episodes share their theory sections and use the same data, so a mixed group can split by tool after the theory and compare numbers at the end (17 supermarkets; tracts selected by intersect / within / centroid: 35 / 6 / 24; about 114,000 city residents by areal weighting, about 77,500 or 68% within 1 mile).
    • The commonest failure is buffering a layer still in EPSG:4326. In QGIS the Buffer dialog then shows “degrees” and a warning sign; in Python GeoPandas prints a geographic CRS warning. Show both on purpose.
    • QGIS: processing results are temporary layers. Learners who close QGIS lose them; remind them to use Make Permanent or save outputs to a GeoPackage if the session has a break.
    • QGIS Buffer defaults to 5 segments; the episode uses 16 to match GeoPandas. With 5, sums differ by well under 1%.
    • Challenge 3 (areal weighting on the Purdue tract) works well as a pair discussion and sets up the Raster Analysis episode (land cover as ancillary data).

    Network Analysis

    • Draw a small graph (four intersections, five roads) before any code.
    • The Case Studies module’s grocery access case study does the same kind of analysis in QGIS, without code. It is a good follow-up, or an alternative for groups that prefer a GUI.
    • ox.nearest_nodes(G, X=lon, Y=lat) takes longitude first. This is the most common bug.
    • add_edge_speeds(G, fallback=40) fills in road types with no speed data. Mention that speeds are estimates from OSM tags, not real traffic.
    • Downloading the network can take up to a minute. Start it, then explain nodes and edges.

    Spatial Autocorrelation with PySAL

    • Every learner needs their own free Census API key. Ask them to request and activate it before the session (it arrives by email). Without it the data cell stops with a clear message.
    • Spatial weights are the hardest idea. Use the chess analogy and a 3 by 3 grid on the board.
    • Stress the p-value filter on LISA maps. Without it, many “hotspots” are noise.
    • Results depend on the units used (counties vs tracts): a good discussion point on the modifiable areal unit problem.

    Spatial Clustering

    • The key lesson is to reproject before clustering. Show that eps=1000 means 1,000 meters only after to_crs(epsg=32616).
    • Crime data reflects reporting and policing as well as crime. Discuss this before showing maps.
    • HDBSCAN now ships with scikit-learn (sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN); the separate hdbscan package is not needed.

    NDVI Analysis

    • Bands are read from GitHub into memory (about 90 MB each). Run the reading cell, then explain NDVI while it loads.
    • The provided bands are Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance. They must be scaled with value * 0.0000275 - 0.2 before computing NDVI.
    • Full resolution images have about 60 million pixels. The notebooks plot every 4th pixel (array[::4, ::4]) so Colab does not run out of memory.
    • The Random Forest example uses stand in labels from NDVI rules, so its near perfect accuracy is not realistic. Point this out, and show how real training polygons would be drawn in QGIS.

    Common problems

    Symptom Likely cause Fix
    NameError: name 'x' is not defined A cell was skipped Runtime > Run before
    HTTPError or a timeout while reading data Network hiccup reading from GitHub or the Census site Rerun the cell
    ModuleNotFoundError: osmnx (or libpysal, rasterio) The !pip install cell did not run Run it, then rerun the imports
    OpenStreetMap download times out Free server busy or rate limited Wait a minute and rerun
    KeyError or HTTP 400 from the Census API Key missing, mistyped or not yet activated Check the key and the activation email
    Map shows “403 Access blocked” or “API key required” behind the points OpenStreetMap and CARTO tiles do not work inside Colab Add tiles="Esri.WorldGrayCanvas" to .explore()
    Colab session crashed Out of memory on a large raster Runtime > Restart session, then rerun
